title: A roadmap towards clinical use of molecular biomarkers in acute ischaemic stroke
title_zh: 分子生物标志物在急性缺血性脑卒中临床应用的路线图
abstract: Acute ischaemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, and even highly effective reperfusion therapies benefit only a fraction of patients. Current clinical decision-making relies largely on clinical examination and imaging, which provide limited insight into the molecular mechanisms that drive injury progression, treatment response and recovery. Molecular biomarkers offer a complementary window into this biology: they can resolve pathway activity at the cellular level, detect pre-morphological tissue stress, report on multi-organ processes and enable high-frequency, minimally invasive monitoring. Here we synthesize emerging evidence across selected, interconnected, outcome-relevant pathomechanisms of acute ischaemic stroke, spanning ischaemic brain injury, metabolism, systemic inflammation and gut dysbiosis. We highlight promising biomarker candidates including brain-derived tau, neurofilament light chain, metabolic and inflammatory signatures and microbiota-derived metabolites and argue that substantial further work is required. In particular, we emphasize the need to prioritize biomarkers as tools for elucidating human stroke pathophysiology rather than focusing solely on therapeutic targets. To guide this effort, we propose a pragmatic, six-phase roadmap from discovery to clinical implementation that emphasizes context of use, assay development, clinical validation and biomarker-guided trials. Applied systematically, mechanism-informed biomarkers could enable more precise, biology-guided stroke care and help to close the translational gap. Clinical decision-making in ischaemic stroke relies mainly on examination and imaging, which offer limited insight into underlying molecular mechanisms. Here, the authors propose a six-phase roadmap for bringing molecular biomarkers into clinical practice, focusing on establishing context of use, assay development, clinical validation and biomarker-guided trials.
abstract_zh: 急性缺血性脑卒中仍然是全球死亡和残疾的主要原因，即使是高度有效的再通疗法也仅惠及一小部分患者。目前的临床决策主要依赖临床检查和影像学，这些方法对驱伤害进展、治疗反应和恢复的分子机制提供了有限的见解。分子生物标志物提供了一个互补的生物学窗口：它们可以细胞水平上解析通路活性、检测非形态学组织应激、报告多器官过程，并实现高频、微创监测。本文综合了急性缺血性脑卒中几个相互关联且与预后相关的病理机制的新兴证据，涵盖缺血性脑损伤、代谢、系统性炎症和肠道菌群失调。我们强调了包括脑源性tau、神经丝轻链、代谢和炎症特征以及源于菌群的代谢物在内的有前景的生物标志物候选者，并论证了需要大量的后续工作。特别是，我们强调将生物标志物作为阐明人类脑卒中病理生理机制的工具的优先性，而不仅仅是治疗靶点。为了指导这项工作，我们提出了一条从发现到临床实施的六阶段路线图，重点在于使用情境、检测方法开发、临床验证和生物标志物指导的临床试验。系统应用机制知情的生物标志物，可以实现更精准的生物学引导的脑卒中护理，并帮助跨越翻译鸿沟。临床决策在缺血性脑卒中主要依赖检查和影像学，这些方法对潜在的分子机制提供了有限的见解。本文作者提出了一条将分子生物标志物引入临床实践的六阶段路线图，重点在于确定使用情境、检测方法开发、临床验证和生物标志物指导的临床试验。
